clue.text: Central to two-part adaptation is tense executive

indicators.note: something central to another thing sits in its middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dramatisation shown in a couple of episodes is a mini-serial
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A boss is pleased with a two-part TV adaptation that is tense.
explanation.walkthrough: MINISERIAL takes T in its exact centre to give MINISTERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministerial describes the executive branch of government, the ministers who carry out policy.

clue.text: Author's sick, sicker, upset in turn about broadcasting Sunset Boulevard?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the flipped words go round the broadcasting term
upset means overturned, and 'in turn' means each word is flipped on its own

parts.note: the writer says I'M, 'I am'
unwell
more unwell
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A writer feels ever sicker watching the film Sunset Boulevard broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the three words is reversed separately, not the whole phrase. Sunset Boulevard is the film, but also a street of rich homes in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Millionaires' Row is a nickname for a street lined with mansions of the very rich, as parts of this Hollywood avenue are.

clue.text: Drink — warming, is it, at daybreak?

definitions.text: Drink — warming, is it, at daybreak?

parts.words: Drink — warming, is it, at daybreak?
parts.note: surface: asks whether a morning drink is a warming one
setter's reading: a hot drink of wine, water and spice, the sort taken to warm up

explanation.surface: Wonders whether some drink taken at dawn will warm you up.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is negus, hot sweetened wine; the parse of 'at daybreak' is uncertain, perhaps sunrise read upward in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is a hot mixture of port or sherry with water, sugar and spice, served as a warming drink.

clue.text: Stock-rider, perhaps the first figure available?

parts.note: a figure is a STAT, and the first one is numbered I
on hand means ready to use

explanation.surface: An Australian stockman is the first person available for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australia a station is a big sheep or cattle farm, and a stock-rider is a mounted herdsman working on one.
explanation.definitionFit: A station hand is a worker on an Australian ranch, and a stock-rider is one such worker.

clue.text: Suspect under cover of some receiver?

indicators.note: a suspect account is dubious, so the letters can't be trusted in their order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the cover of something is its outside, so only its two outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A suspect operating undercover as a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' and 'receiver' paint a fence for stolen goods; receiver is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The end-user is the final recipient of a product or service, the person who actually gets and uses it.

clue.text: Man's son maybe confirmed to be big hit

parts.note: answering 'it is' confirms a question
a lander is a heavy blow that lands

explanation.surface: A man's son has been confirmed as a big success.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, so its son is a native of the island.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Isle of Man lives on an island, so is an islander.

clue.text: O setter, O setter's setter? I'm part of a package

parts.note: O is zero, love in tennis
the setter refers to himself
again zero in tennis
belonging to the setter
a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: A cryptic string of O's and setters, as if the compiler talks about himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The last 'setter' is the dog breed. The proverb means accepting someone means taking their faults or attachments too.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying says the speaker comes as a bundle with their pet or flaws, so 'I'm part of a package' captures it.

clue.text: Top 23 people long to start holding mass

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so the phrase surrounds the extra letter

parts.note: men are people
to ache for is to long for
M is the physics abbreviation for mass
to begin is to start

explanation.surface: Leading people from somewhere are keen to begin a Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top 23' means the leading figure among the answer at 23 Across. 'Holding' puts the mass letter inside the joined words, between the second and third.
explanation.definitionFit: Menachem Begin was Prime Minister of Israel, so a top Israeli politician.

clue.text: Revelling in a barrister's whimsy

indicators.note: revelling suggests wild partying, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: all the letters, including the possessive S

explanation.surface: A lawyer's partying is a sign of capricious behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitrariness is acting on impulse rather than reason, which is the nature of whimsy.

clue.text: Content of dialogue's moving tributes

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift out of their original order
the content of something is what lies inside its edges, so the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: the word with its outside letters removed

explanation.surface: Speeches within a dialogue are moving tributes to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' reads as touching, but it is the signal to rearrange. EULOGIA is a plural of eulogium.
explanation.definitionFit: Eulogia are formal speeches or writings praising a person, which are tributes paid to them.

clue.text: Did abuse in retreat hit home here?

indicators.note: a word in retreat goes backwards, so its letters are read from the end

parts.note: to revile is to abuse verbally; past tense

explanation.surface: Asks whether a retreating army that abused people was struck at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: to deliver a blow is to make it hit home, and the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a punch or a message is to land it so that it strikes its target squarely.

clue.text: Is mad rolling joints where crewmen are most likely to see you?

definitions.text: where crewmen are most likely to see you

indicators.note: something rolling tumbles over, so these letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: the two words rearranged
hips are joints of the body

explanation.surface: Someone rolling joints is asked whether they're mad, as the crew will catch them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling joints' looks like a single drug-taking image, but rolling is the anagram signal and joints are body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidships means in the middle of a vessel, the busiest part of the deck where sailors work.

clue.text: Clouds #3 for Joni; #1 is AC/DC

indicators.note: number three points to the third letter of the following name

parts.note: third letter of the name
number one is myself, so 'number one is' is I'M
AC/DC is slang for bisexual, shortened to BI

explanation.surface: Reads like a chart listing: Joni Mitchell's album Clouds at number three, AC/DC at number one.
explanation.walkthrough: Clouds is a Joni Mitchell album and AC/DC a rock band, but here AC/DC is old slang for bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi is the plural of nimbus, the grey rain-bearing cloud.

clue.text: See 3 Down
Barrier Reef explorer who has items at market? Aussie's dug in

indicators.note: the slang word is dug into the middle of the trader, sitting inside it

parts.note: one offering goods at market
nork is Australian slang for a breast; a dug is an udder or teat

explanation.surface: A stallholder exploring the Great Barrier Reef, where an Australian has dug in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug in' looks like digging; dug is an old word for a breast or teat, and NORK is its Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitors explore the Great Barrier Reef by swimming face-down with a breathing tube, which makes them snorkellers.

clue.text: Lonely chap of note working on the butter mountain? …

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the solitary herdsman of a famous yodelling song in The Sound of Music
second meaning: a butter is a beast that butts, so this is someone tending such animals on an alpine slope

explanation.surface: A famously lonely man employed at the European butter surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'butter mountain' was the EU's stockpile of surplus butter; here a butter is an animal that butts. 'The Lonely Goatherd' is the Sound of Music song.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman of nannies and billies is named in a Rodgers and Hammerstein song, and tends butting animals on mountainsides.

clue.text: Flat area is undivided, Times writer claims

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the writer holds the other pieces

parts.note: the setter, as writer, refers to himself as me
A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written
undivided means one, in one piece
T is time, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A newspaper journalist claims a flat area hasn't been split up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times writer' suggests a journalist at that paper, but Times is TT and writer is ME, wrapping everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a self-contained flat, often on two floors of a larger building.

clue.text: … Honoured retirees not alone in flourishing Maine-et-Loire

indicators.note: flourishing suggests something waved about with a flourish, so the letters are scrambled
'not' tells us the following word is taken away from the fodder

parts.note: the French department name, taken letter by letter
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: Retired dignitaries living together in the French Loire region, following on from the lonely goatherd.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link it to 15 Down: unlike the lonely goatherd, these are 'not alone'. Removing those letters leaves seven to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are retired professors or clergy who keep their title as a mark of honour.

clue.text: Idling teacher's work done?

parts.note: a teacher marking puts ticks on correct answers
finished, at an end

explanation.surface: Asks whether a lazy teacher's work is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idling' seems to describe the teacher, but it is the definition, as of an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine ticking over runs slowly without moving the vehicle, which is what idling means.

clue.text: See 18 Down
The finale of the opening race

indicators.note: a finale comes at the end, so only the last letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word
a vent is an opening for air or gas

explanation.surface: Suggests a race meeting's first race also served as its climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The finale' and 'the opening' sound like parts of a show; finale picks a letter and opening is a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is one contest in a sports programme, such as a single race at an athletics meeting.

clue.text: Expert on duty calls reserve back about error

indicators.note: back tells us to read everything before it from its end

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: about means around, so the reserve goes round the mistake

parts.note: ice means coolness or reserve in manner
a cross marks a mistake

explanation.surface: A specialist on call names a reserve player after an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert on duty' sounds like whoever is on shift, but duty here is the tax on goods, which an exciseman collected.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciseman was a revenue officer who assessed and collected excise, the tax levied on goods.

clue.text: American guy's wrapped selection from Japanese takeaway?

indicators.note: something wrapped is enclosed by an outer layer, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: belonging to a man
abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: An American man's choice from a Japanese takeaway comes wrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The man's word turns round so its last letter comes first, then holds the country inside it, much as sushi rolls are wrapped in seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi, vinegared rice with fish, is one of the dishes you might pick from a Japanese takeaway menu.

clue.text: Retired Limerick man's enthralled by couple from Jerusalem?

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
to be enthralled by something is to be captured and held inside it

parts.note: two, written as the Roman numeral
Edward Lear popularised the limerick; possessive

explanation.surface: A retired Irishman from Limerick is charmed by a couple from Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limerick man' suggests an Irishman from that city, but it is Edward Lear, writer of limericks.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerusalem is claimed as Israel's capital, so someone from there is Israeli; the question mark admits it is only an example.

clue.text: Shameful act on fateful day: finally Brutus moved to pierce Caesar's?

indicators.note: the letter at the head is moved along to the back of its word

parts.note: a sin is a shameful act
the Ides of March, the day Caesar was murdered
points at the letter that moves: the S at the head of the first piece, which is also the last letter of the conspirator's name

explanation.surface: Recounts Caesar's assassination on the Ides of March, Brutus finally moved to stab him.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN is placed on IDES, then its S, the final letter of Brutus, moves to the back of SIN, giving INS + IDES.
explanation.definitionFit: The question asks what Brutus pierced: Caesar's internal organs, his guts, which is what insides means.

clue.text: Status symbol Spooner's given speedy player at the Madejski?

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds trade places

parts.note: the Madejski Stadium is home to Reading FC, and a fast player there plays on the wing

explanation.surface: A footballer's status symbol as a fast winger for a club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Madejski Stadium was Reading FC's ground; Reading is pronounced 'redding', so swapping R and W works.
explanation.definitionFit: The band worn on the finger shows a person's marital status, so it is a symbol of being married.
